newsitem.title: USA: Calif. pension system names new investment officer.
newsitem.headline: Calif. pension system names new investment officer.

text.p: SACRAMENTO, Calif. - California's $68 billion State Teachers' Retirement System (Calstrs) will replace its veteran chief investment officer with Patrick Mitchell following months of controversy over the fund's returns.

Mitchell will replace Tom Flanigan, who has held the chief investment officer position for 11 years, Calstrs said. Mitchell, 48, has worked at Calstrs since 1988 and currently serves as its director of fixed income and equities.

"Patrick Mitchell is an extremely talented investment professional and is highly regarded by the investment management community," said Emma Zink, the retirement board's chairwoman. "The priority will be to continue the fund's long term growth and diversification in a prudent manner."
The Calstrs shake-up, announced on Friday, was not a surprise. Top state finance officials have for months been critical of the pension fund's investment performance.
